props.title: I Like It Like That

sections.content: **I Like It Like That (1994)** (1994) blazed new ground as the first major studio film directed by a Latina (Darnell Martin). This vibrant slice-of-life drama set in the South Bronx captures the energy and challenges of a young Puerto Rican family with raw authenticity. Like Spike Lee's **Do the Right Thing** (1989) and **Jungle Fever** (1991), Martin's film brings an electric urban energy while tackling issues of race, gender, and class through a distinctly New York lens. The film launched Luna Lauren Velez's career with her magnetic performance as Lisette Linares.

sections.content: The mid-1990s marked a crucial period for Latinx representation in American cinema. While **La Bamba** (1987) and **Stand and Deliver** (1988) had made earlier inroads, films like **I Like It Like That** (1994) and **Mi Vida Loca** (1993) brought authentic voices telling contemporary urban stories. Martin's direction particularly shines in capturing the vibrant community life of the Bronx, from the street scenes to the intimate family moments, establishing a template that influenced later films like **In the Heights** (2021).

The film's exploration of gender dynamics within Latinx culture was groundbreaking for its time. Like Girlfight (2000) and Real Women Have Curves (2002), it presents a complex female protagonist fighting against traditional expectations. Lisette's journey from housewife to model while dealing with her husband Chino's machismo reflects tensions still relevant today, handled with nuance rather than stereotypes. sections.content: Martin's directorial style influenced a wave of authentic urban storytelling in the late 1990s and early 2000s. Films like **Our Song** (2000) and Raising Victor Vargas (2002) followed similar verite-style approaches to capturing city life. The film's success also helped pave the way for more Latina directors, though progress remained slow - it would take until **Fast Food Nation** (2006) for Patricia Cardoso to direct another major studio release.
